te: 3 Land Transport bills: decentralising to provinces and local government
se: The committee studied 3 versions of the Land Transport Bill (No. ..) B.E. .... under rule 119. Their core is decentralising the oversight of land transport to provincial committees and local administrative organisations. The Cabinet's version gives provincial committees more power to set routes, fares and passenger terminals in the province, while a version proposed by members of the House of Representatives would, for example, let the Department of Land Transport step in when a local government cannot run a bus terminal. The committee also discussed promoting seaplanes.
it: Land Transport Bill (No. ..) B.E. .... (3 versions) under rule 119
Promoting seaplanes

te: Meeting summary video · 3 Land Transport bills: decentralising to provinces and local government
Aviation fees and links to secondary cities: a working group is set up
se: The committee studied the structure of aviation fees and service charges to promote the air transport network and meet growing travel demand, with the Ministry of Transport, the Department of Airports, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand, Airports of Thailand, Aeronautical Radio of Thailand and the Civil Aviation Training Center invited. The agencies explained ways to promote the use of airports, such as fee reductions. The committee resolved to set up a working group to study the matter in detail within 60 days and make recommendations.
it: Structure of aviation fees and service charges to promote the air transport network
Setting up a working group (60 days)

te: Meeting summary video · Aviation fees and links to secondary cities: a working group is set up
Tourist railway along Highway 44, Surat Thani–Krabi, is economically worthwhile
se: The committee considered the subcommittee's report, which studied using land along national Highway 44 (Southern Seaboard) between Surat Thani and Krabi, where land has already been expropriated with a right of way of about 200 metres. It proposes a railway of about 100 kilometres with 9 stations, focusing on tourism and services and able to carry farm produce. The study found the project economically worthwhile, with an economic internal rate of return (EIRR) of 7.82 per cent, a net present value of 1,564 million baht and a benefit–cost ratio of 1.12. The committee agreed to submit the report to the Senate.
it: Study report on infrastructure linking the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea (railway along Highway 44)

te: Meeting summary video · Tourist railway along Highway 44, Surat Thani–Krabi, is economically worthwhile
Report on safety in building infrastructure: safety costs must not be cut
se: The committee considered the report of the subcommittee studying safety measures in building land and rail infrastructure. Serious accidents in large construction projects in 2024–2026 were mainly caused by not strictly following safety measures and by contract terms not being enforced strictly enough. The report proposes raising safety across the whole life of a project, from design and construction to maintenance, setting safety costs as a separate fixed item so they are not cut in price competition, and having a central body to investigate transport accidents. The committee also considered a study visit to Mae Hong Son.
it: Report on safety measures in building land and rail infrastructure
Study visit to Mae Hong Son

te: Digital logistics report: one-stop data, joint tickets and truck weighing
se: The committee considered the subcommittee's report, which proposes reforming the government's digital infrastructure so that transport and logistics are more efficient and transparent, solving the problem of data kept separately by each agency through 3 projects: the National Single Window, the joint ticket system, and smart technology to control truck weights. It proposes submitting data only once (Single Submission) and a central data platform that can be checked afterwards, reducing discretion and duplication. The committee also considered setting up a subcommittee and appointing people to assist the committee.
it: Study report on digital logistics (National Single Window, joint tickets, truck weights)
Setting up a subcommittee and appointing assistants

te: Study of Highway 44, Krabi–Surat Thani, completed, and northern study visits planned
se: The subcommittee studying the potential of transport infrastructure linking the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea, Krabi–Surat Thani, reported that it held its last meeting on 3 September 2026 and has completed its study, and is now writing the report, focusing on the potential of Highway 44 for further infrastructure. The committee also considered the schedule for study visits to Mae Hong Son–Chiang Mai and to Nan.
it: Findings on infrastructure linking the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea (Highway 44)
Schedule for study visits to Mae Hong Son–Chiang Mai and Nan

te: Construction safety on M82–Rama 2 Road, and progress of the subcommittees
se: The subcommittee studying safety measures in building land and rail infrastructure reported that its study is complete and the report is being prepared. Its visit to the M82 project on Rama 2 Road found issues such as temporary safety systems, too little lighting because power cables had been stolen, and drivers going faster than the limit, so it proposed that agencies step up monitoring. The committee also heard progress from the subcommittees on logistics and on infrastructure linking the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea (Highway 44).
it: Progress of the subcommittee on construction safety (M82, Rama 2 Road)
Progress of the subcommittees on logistics and on Gulf of Thailand–Andaman links

te: Results of the visit on border transport links at Mukdahan–Savannakhet
se: The committee considered the results of the study visit on 13–15 August 2026 to Nakhon Phanom, Mukdahan and Lao PDR. The committee met the Deputy Governor of Mukdahan and the agencies concerned at the provincial hall about the progress and obstacles of transport networks, logistics and the management of border checkpoints, and proposed that agencies work together and speed up key projects. It also heard the report of the subcommittee on digital logistics about the National Single Window.
it: Results of the study visit to Nakhon Phanom–Mukdahan–Lao PDR
Report of the logistics subcommittee (National Single Window)

te: Preparing a study visit to Nakhon Phanom–Mukdahan–Lao PDR
se: The committee approved the schedule for a study visit to Nakhon Phanom, Mukdahan and the Lao People's Democratic Republic on 13–15 August 2026, to follow transport and infrastructure projects that benefit the public, and heard progress on work in which the committee's representatives take part.
it: Schedule for the study visit to Nakhon Phanom–Mukdahan–Lao PDR (13–15 August 2026)
Progress of work with committee representatives

te: Planning visits to Mukdahan and Chiang Rai–Mae Hong Son, and following work with committee representatives
se: Meeting on Wednesday 22 July 2026 (moved from 15 July). The committee set study visits to Mukdahan on 13–15 August 2026 and to Chiang Rai–Mae Hong Son on 16–19 September 2026, and heard progress on work in which the committee's representatives take part, such as the Annual Appropriations Bill for fiscal year 2027 and background checks of people nominated for office, as well as follow-up on rail transport law.
it: Schedule for study visits to Mukdahan and Chiang Rai–Mae Hong Son
Progress of work with committee representatives (2027 budget and consideration of nominees)

te: Navigation in Thai Waters bill: adding search and rescue
se: The committee studied the Navigation in Thai Waters Bill (No. ..) B.E. ...., which updates the existing law by adding provisions on searching for and rescuing people in distress at sea, in line with international obligations, using the structures and mechanisms of existing agencies. The committee agreed in principle with the bill proposed by the Cabinet and asked the secretariat to draft the report.
it: Navigation in Thai Waters Bill (No. ..) B.E. .... (search and rescue)

te: Study of 3 electric train expropriation bills
se: The committee studied the bills on expropriating property to build electric trains and on placing charges on property for mass transit, for the Yellow and Pink Lines, which are already in service. After hearing the agencies concerned, it agreed in principle with the bills proposed by the Cabinet and asked the secretariat to draft the study report.
it: Bills on expropriation and charges on property (3 bills)
